areaDescription: A mist-choked stretch of shoreline where salt spray clings to black stone and gulls cry through the fog like distant warnings. Hidden coves, half-sunk wrecks, and weather-softened paths make the coast feel unsettled rather than truly perilous, though travelers still tread carefully in its shifting veils.

map.notes: Extended schema with AI-friendly navigation fields

locations.name: Veiled Memory Passage
locations.description: A narrow black-stone corridor where cold mist crawls along the floor in ankle-high ribbons. Salt crystals glaze the walls like old tears, and carved elven lines repeat in looping sequences that subtly change whenever no one is looking directly at them.

npcs.name: Lethariel Vaun, a wary wardkeeper scout
npcs.description: A cautious scout stationed here to watch for intruders who follow the wrong memories. She marks safe stone with chalk and warns that the corridor's inscriptions can be trusted only after they are spoken aloud.

npcs.name: Ilyra Fen, a frightened witness with fragmented memories
npcs.description: Ilyra clutches a broken shell pendant and repeatedly loses track of which passage she came from. She can describe flashes of hidden doors, but only if the party calms her and helps piece together her memories.

lootTable: 1d4 healing potions hidden in a dry niche
plotHooks: The repeating inscriptions hint at a memory-locked route deeper into Numillian.
Lethariel can reveal that the passage only stays stable when travelers speak the correct names of nearby places.
Ilyra's fragments point toward a chamber where the city tests intruders with mirrored illusions.
locations.dmInstructions: Use this corridor as the connective tissue between the coast approach and the trials beyond. The writing should subtly foreshadow the city's reliance on memory, naming, and spoken truth.

doors.name: South Arch
doors.description: A broad arched opening veiled by hanging mist and salt-stiffened kelp strands.

doors.name: East Stone Door
doors.description: A smooth slab of black stone etched with a tide spiral that seems to rotate when viewed from the corner of the eye.

traps.name: Memory Slip Glyph
traps.description: A faint rune in the floor causes a traveler to misremember the last ten feet of movement, risking a stumble into the wrong side passage.
traps.damage: No damage; the creature is pushed 10 feet and has disadvantage on its next Perception check

dcChecks: Investigation DC 13: Notice the corridor's inscriptions rewrite themselves in response to spoken names.
Arcana DC 14: Identify the memory-slip effect before it disorients the party.
Insight DC 12: Determine that Ilyra's fragments are genuine but incomplete.
locations.accessibility: Normal access; the passage is open but its shifting inscriptions can mislead the unwary.

features.name: Shifting Inscription Bands
features.description: Lines of elven script loop around the walls and subtly alter their wording when not directly observed.

features.name: Salt-Fog Drift
features.description: Low mist pools in the corridor, muffling footsteps and making the space feel larger than it is.

features.name: Chalk Mark Niche
features.description: A shallow recess where prior wardkeepers have left safety marks, arrows, and warnings.

encounters.name: Misdirected Footsteps
encounters.description: If the party ignores the inscriptions, the corridor briefly loops them back to its midpoint, forcing them to reorient before proceeding.

locations.adventureSummary: The Veiled Memory Passage introduces the coast's deceptive calm and establishes the theme of truth spoken aloud. It links the outer approach to the trial spaces and provides the first hints that memory itself is part of the city's defenses.

locations.name: Gleaming Tribute Vault
locations.description: A low chamber lined with polished black stone and shallow alcoves for offerings. The air smells of brine and old incense, and dozens of reflective inlays catch even the dimmest light, making the room glitter like a tide of coins.

npcs.name: Elarion Sableleaf, a diplomatic wardkeeper envoy
npcs.description: An envoy tasked with preserving the vault's social protocols as carefully as its seals. He insists that any tribute taken must be balanced by a spoken oath or a returned favor.

npcs.name: Thalan Deepcurrent, a trapped maintenance mage
npcs.description: Trapped behind a collapsed service grate, Thalan can describe the vault's maintenance routes and hidden fail-safes. He is anxious, brilliant, and desperate to be freed before the wards recycle the chamber.

plotHooks: Elarion explains that tribute vaults in Numillian are tied to civic memory and cannot simply be looted without consequence.
Thalan knows a maintenance phrase that can suppress one ward for a short time.
A hidden niche contains a record of prior visitors whose names were erased from the city's memory.
locations.dmInstructions: This is a social-and-treasure room rather than a simple hoard. Reward respectful interaction, but make greedy behavior awaken the vault's defensive echoes or trigger a ward response.

doors.name: West Arch
doors.description: An open archway bordered by sea-glass tiles, leading back toward the memory passage.

doors.name: North Vault Door
doors.description: A heavy circular door with concentric rings and a central tribute slot shaped like a handprint.
doors.trap: If forced without the proper token, a burst of radiant salt sparks fills the doorway.

traps.name: Tribute Echo
traps.description: Taking valuables without speaking the vault's acknowledgement phrase causes the chamber to ring with accusatory echoes that reveal the thief's position.
traps.damage: 2d6 thunder damage and the creature is outlined by shimmering light until the end of its next turn

dcChecks: Persuasion DC 13: Secure Elarion's cooperation and learn the vault etiquette.
Investigation DC 14: Find the hidden maintenance grate where Thalan is trapped.
Arcana DC 15: Recognize the tribute echo as a warded alarm rather than a damaging curse.
locations.accessibility: Normal access, though the north vault door requires a tribute token or clever bypass.

features.name: Reflective Inlays
features.description: Polished stone panels reflect movement a half-second late, creating an unsettling sense of doubled motion.

features.name: Tribute Alcoves
features.description: Small niches around the room once held offerings, oaths, and memory seals.

features.name: Collapsed Maintenance Grate
features.description: A bent iron grate reveals a cramped service space where someone can be heard shifting behind the wall.

encounters.name: Ward Echo Response
encounters.description: If the vault is disturbed improperly, the room animates with harmless but obstructive echo-images of wardkeepers that try to drive intruders toward the exit.

locations.adventureSummary: The Gleaming Tribute Vault offers treasure, etiquette, and a trapped ally who can teach the party how Numillian's civic magic works. It also reinforces that wealth here is bound to memory, obligation, and spoken protocol.

locations.name: Forbidden Echo Vault
locations.description: A sealed chamber of dark mirror-stone and suspended hush. Every sound seems to return a heartbeat later, altered by the room's lingering enchantments, and a pale seam of light traces the outline of a deeper lock set into the far wall.

npcs.name: Maerith the Unseen, cabal strategist
npcs.description: A hidden strategist who has already infiltrated the vault's periphery and now manipulates events through projected whispers and false reflections. Maerith is never where they seem to be, but their plans are written across the room's mirrored surfaces.

npcs.name: High Warden Selvaris, final authority over the vault wards
npcs.description: The ultimate voice of the vault's security, appearing here in person or as a ward-projected overseer depending on how the party arrives. Selvaris will demand identification, then test whether the intruders are thieves, petitioners, or liabilities.

plotHooks: The vault seam leads to a deeper sanctum and confirms that the forbidden power lies beyond this chamber.
Maerith's manipulation suggests a rival faction is trying to trigger the vault's release mechanisms.
Selvaris can be persuaded to grant limited access if the party proves the deeper threat is worse than the intrusion.
locations.dmInstructions: This should feel like the threshold of a major secret. Keep the encounter tense and intelligent: Selvaris may bargain, Maerith may taunt from cover, and the guardians should defend the seam to the deeper sanctum rather than fight to the death.

doors.name: South Gate
doors.description: A reinforced stone gate framed by mirror-black ribs and etched with ward sigils.
doors.trap: A pulse of force and echoing disorientation erupts when opened without authorization.

doors.name: Deep Seam Panel
doors.description: A nearly invisible panel in the far wall where the stone looks thinner, as if it were stretched over a hidden passage.

traps.name: Echo Reversal Ward
traps.description: A ward causes hostile sounds to bounce back at their source, turning shouted commands and spellcasting into a risk for the unwary.
traps.damage: 3d6 thunder damage and the creature is deafened until the end of its next turn

dcChecks: Insight DC 15: Tell when Selvaris is speaking from authority versus when a ward is speaking through them.
Arcana DC 16: Identify the mirror seam as a gateway mechanism tied to forbidden vault wards.
Perception DC 17: Spot Maerith's hidden vantage point among the reflections.
locations.accessibility: Restricted access; the vault is sealed and can be approached only by passing the previous chamber's defenses or obtaining ward authority.

features.name: Mirror-Stone Walls
features.description: The chamber's reflective surfaces distort silhouettes and make it difficult to tell which movement is real.

features.name: Suspended Silence
features.description: Sound dulls here, then returns late and warped, making conversation feel like a negotiation with the room itself.

features.name: Deep Seam of Light
features.description: A pale vertical line in the far wall suggests a path into the forbidden sanctum beyond.

encounters.name: Ward Authority Challenge
encounters.description: Selvaris demands proof of intent while Maerith attempts to destabilize the chamber with false commands and reflection tricks.

locations.adventureSummary: The Forbidden Echo Vault is the climax of the coast approach, combining elite guardianship, political tension, and the first clear route into the forbidden sanctum. It should feel like the final gate before the party enters the city's deepest secrets.

locations.name: Tidebound Riddle Chamber
locations.description: A circular chamber where the floor is carved like a tide pool map and the walls are inscribed with layered riddles in faded gold. At the center stands a low stone dais with four grooves, each shaped like a different spoken answer rather than a physical key.

npcs.name: Sister Aelwyn, a masked city oracle
npcs.description: A masked oracle who speaks in tidal metaphors and reveals answers only when the party asks the right question. She understands the chamber's riddles and warns that incorrect certainty is more dangerous than ignorance.

npcs.name: Arannis Vey, keeper of the trial chambers
npcs.description: The chamber's official overseer, responsible for judging whether an answer is sincere, clever, or merely stolen. Arannis watches from the dais or a side alcove and may offer a trial instead of a fight.

npcs.name: Mirael of the Third Reflection, an illusion-bound examiner
npcs.description: An examiner bound to the chamber's mirrored judgments, appearing in a surface of still water or polished stone. Mirael tests the party with layered illusions and can reveal hidden truths if properly engaged.

plotHooks: The chamber's answers point toward the deeper trial spaces in the Hall of Memory Trials.
A correct response unlocks a hidden route and provides the party with a memory-safe phrase.
Arannis and Mirael can jointly confirm which rumors about Numillian are true and which are planted lies.
locations.dmInstructions: This is the puzzle-forward location that bridges exploration and roleplay. Let the riddles be solvable through observation, conversation, or prior clues from the coast, and reward players who ask the oracle the right questions instead of guessing.

doors.name: West Arch
doors.description: A low arch with wave motifs and worn steps leading back to the passage.

doors.name: East Riddle Gate
doors.description: A round stone gate with four answer grooves and no visible handle.

traps.name: False Answer Pulse
traps.description: Speaking an incorrect answer aloud causes the chamber to emit a sharp pulse that scrambles the speaker's recent memory of the riddle.
traps.damage: 2d6 psychic damage and the creature cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn

dcChecks: Investigation DC 14: Learn which carvings are original and which are added later.
Religion DC 13: Recognize Sister Aelwyn's ritual masking as a sign of sanctioned oracle status.
Arcana DC 15: Understand how Mirael's reflections bind the chamber's illusion tests.
locations.accessibility: Accessible with caution; the chamber is open, but progression depends on solving the riddle gate or earning the overseers' approval.

features.name: Tide-Map Floor
features.description: The floor depicts a coastline that shifts depending on where the viewer stands, implying different answers to the same question.

features.name: Answer Grooves
features.description: Four carved slots on the dais respond to spoken truths rather than inserted keys.

features.name: Still-Water Mirror
features.description: A shallow basin in the center reflects people with slight delays, as if judging their honesty.

encounters.name: Trial of the Spoken Tide
encounters.description: The chamber challenges the party to answer a sequence of riddles or present a convincing case for why they should be allowed to proceed.

locations.adventureSummary: The Tidebound Riddle Chamber is the module's puzzle and lore hub, where the city's trial culture comes into focus. It opens the way toward the Hall of Memory Trials while teaching the party that words, not force, are often the real keys in Numillian.
